description:
LANDED 8c3d5ce90 on wt/kdt13-boundaries (2026-09-02; base 172ab21f1;
one commit, 23 files +~1100/-~300 incl. 3 new behaviour fixtures).
Refuter FIX-THEN-MERGE, four findings folded before merge; coordinator
gate COORD-GATE-1788383942: fmt clean, release build 0 warnings, clippy
-D warnings clean, cargo test --lib 1583/0/5, fixture_matrix
--test-threads=1 485/0/9 (known-red names unchanged: enum_tier0,
enumerable_protocol_dispatch, fz_f98_map_reduce x run/interp/build).

WHAT LANDED. RuntimeTypePredicate.callables is CallableShapes { targets
(derived), shapes, exact } over CallableShape { target, captures:
[RuntimeTypePredicate] } -- fz-kdt.119's TupleShapes twin; AxisPrecision
for callables is PerPosition and axis_erases recurses into captures.
Admission of a VALUE is CONTAINMENT (CallableShape::inside, capture-wise
RuntimeTypePredicate::contained_in -- containment of tests); arm TESTS
relate by overlap / erasing-overlap. The projection keeps lit.captures;
how a clause projects is decided in ONE place
(Types::runtime_type_predicate_callables); the envelope keeps the clause
shape it is handed (a multi-literal clause degrades to target_only in
both paths -- the refuter's F1, folded with two pins in types_test.rs);
an anonymous literal reaches CallableShapes::any() -- the seam
fz-kdt.127.2 needs. Native: NativeCallableBoundary gains `callable` +
`shape`, loses `target`; callable_addresses ORs the boundaries the test
enumerates. Interp: backend_callable_identity answers with the wrapper's
shape. Prim::ClosureCapture carries `constructions: Box<[FnId]>` (the
minting wrappers' identity_fns); lower_closure_capture reads the repr
from those, agreement kept as a tripwire over exactly them (fz-kdt.157's
refusing half now has a reachable red witness).

DELETED (grep-proven 0 hits in src/ and .agent/): the captures:
Vec::new() erasure in callable_identity_clauses (survives only in
fn_ref_lit, correctly); callable_boundaries_for_target + "has to admit
all of them"; NativeCallableBoundary.target and the surface copy; dead
capture_key; the per-FnId agreement rule; the interp wrapper exemption
(CONSTRUCTION_WRAPPER_IDENTITY_BASE == 0); FiniteSet<ClosureTarget> as
the axis field and the Fn(u64)->Option<ClosureTarget> resolver
signature; "honest only while" (both copies); INDISTINGUISHABLE_ARM_
RESIDUE and its pin (its five fixtures promoted into the zero gate);
"leave no trace" / "one code pointer is one question" doctrine; unused
imports. Gates re-homed: a_nested_callables_captures_are_A_question
(inverted); runtime_indistinguishable_arms_keep_the_order_they_arrived_in
re-homed on %{a: int} vs %{a: float} (a map test is an Erasing kind
check, genuinely one question).

FIXTURES (all three doors, Elixir oracles): same_lambda_two_capture_
types.fz (RED at base: interp 12.0 11.0 11.0 12.0, native refusal;
GREEN: 12 11.0 11.0 12); same_lambda_two_capture_types_dynamic.fz
(green at base and head; NO question at this stage -- no callsite has
two targets; it is 127.2's regression guard, the review's "shape test at
run's callsite under (B)" row was inferred, not measured); callable_
union_capture_containment.fz (12 11.0 12 11.0; under an overlap swap
interp 12.0 and JIT aborts in fz_closure_get_capture_f64 -- fz-kdt.167
folded and closed).

MOVEMENT (596 fixtures x 3 doors, base vs head): behaviour 0 movers
besides the new fixtures (28 differing files normalize to thread ids /
ASLR / a shifted panic line in fixtures panicking identically at base);
canon 9 movers = the predicted set (00231, 00275, 00277, 00281, a_mixed,
closure_identity_captures, enum_predicate_search, opaque_fn_value_join,
repr_seam_enum_count_after_reduce2), executable and dispatch-node counts
unchanged on every one, +2/+4 questions or text-only capture types in
question strings; a_mixed reseats wide-first (sound; base had no question
and the exact body took everything; grounded x23 now dead-but-emitted =
fz-kdt.168's first live instance). Stress lens 7 settings x 3 doors x
20 programs: 0 movers; corpus interp: 0. FIFO/LIFO mover set identical
to base. Double-compile byte-identical. Wall clock max 0.43s (base
0.44s). Three projections of a capture (arm / native / interp) agree on
every construction in the corpus (refuter instrument, 0 disagreements).

REFUTER PROBES (11, all correct on 3 doors): union-typed capture; capture
that is a closure of two identities; mailbox any capture beside int/float
constructions; atom-tagged tuple and list captures; two- and five-deep
nesting; fnref vs zero-capture closure of one function; mailbox closures
into capture-bearing arms. New defect found OUTSIDE this change:
fz-kdt.170 (map-typed capture at two value types wrong at base and head).

DOCS: dispatch-matrix.md callable paragraphs, AxisPrecision row, the 119
nested example (two observables), the multi-literal degrade; pipeline.md
construction-identity paragraph; surface.rs / types/mod.rs /
runtime_type_predicate.rs doc comments; fz-kdt.125's record corrected.

comments.text:
BUILT, one commit f34c2aaa3 on wt/kdt127-1-build (base 172ab21f1),
16 files +1032/-297 plus 6 new fixture files.

WHAT LANDED, against the spec. `RuntimeTypePredicate.callables` is
`CallableShapes { targets (derived), shapes, exact }` over
`CallableShape { target, captures: [RuntimeTypePredicate] }`, the
`TupleShapes` twin; the precision row is PerPosition and `axis_erases`
recurses into captures. Admission of a VALUE is CONTAINMENT
(`CallableShape::inside`, capture-wise `contained_in`), arm TESTS relate
by overlap / erasing-overlap. Projection keeps `lit.captures` in both
`callable_identity_clauses` and the new
`Types::runtime_type_predicate_callables`; an anonymous literal has no
clause to shape and reaches `CallableShapes::any()` -- the seam
fz-kdt.127.2 needs. Native `NativeCallableBoundary` gains `callable` and
`shape`, loses `target`; `callable_addresses` ORs the boundaries the test
ENUMERATES. Interp `backend_callable_identity` answers with the wrapper's
shape. `Prim::ClosureCapture` carries `constructions: Box<[FnId]>` (the
minting wrappers' identity_fns -- a CallableId would invert the
fz_ir->compiler2 layering) and `lower_closure_capture` reads the repr
from those, keeping the agreement check as a tripwire over exactly them.

GATES, all fresh from the final tree, markers quoted.
GATE-1788380187: `cargo fmt --check` clean; `cargo build --release` 0
warnings (forced, `touch src/lib.rs`); `cargo clippy --all-targets --
-D warnings` clean (verified to lint the lib-test target by planting an
`unused_variables` violation in drive_test.rs and watching it error).
GATE-1788380215: `cargo test --lib compiler2::` 1305 passed / 0 failed /
5 ignored; `cargo test --lib` 1581 / 0 / 5.
GATE-1788380346: `cargo test --test fixture_matrix -- --test-threads=1`
482 passed / 0 failed / 9 ignored (base 476/0/9; +6 = the two new
fixtures x 3 paths). The 9 ignored are enum_tier0, fz_f98_map_reduce and
enumerable_protocol_dispatch x {run, interp, build}, and the fixture
`defer.*` headers they come from are byte-identical to 172ab21f1's.

RED FIRST, measured by me at base (RED-1788378579, base binary rebuilt
from a `git archive 172ab21f1` tree verified byte-identical to HEAD's
src). `same_lambda_two_capture_types.fz`: interp `12.0 11.0 11.0 12.0`
where the Elixir oracle says `12 11.0 11.0 12` -- BOTH call orders wrong;
`fz2 run` and `fz2 build` refuse with "closure capture 0 of callable 73
has no single settled representation". At head, all three doors print the
oracle's four lines. `same_lambda_two_capture_types_dynamic.fz` is green
at base and at head.

RED FIRST for the two new lib gates, by reverting the mechanism.
Restoring the single deleted `captures: Vec::new()` line in
`callable_identity_clauses` turns
`compiler2_a_forwarded_lambdas_capture_layout_is_the_runtime_question`
red and the fixture wrong again (interp 12.0; JIT now faults at
`fz_closure_get_capture_f64 expected float, got Int(1)` -- the misroute
itself, which the construction-keyed unpack lets through to run).
Loosening `constructions_minting` to "any construction of the same
function" turns
`compiler2_a_capture_unpack_reads_the_constructions_that_minted_its_layout`
red and makes the native door refuse the fixture -- fz-kdt.157's refusing
half now has a program that reaches it.

MOVEMENT, three doors x 594 fixtures, base vs head sweeps taken with the
two binaries in this session. 28 output files differ; 25 are process/
thread ids, ASLR backtrace addresses, and one panic LINE NUMBER shifted
by this diff (jobs/native.rs 3424 -> 3443) inside fixtures that panic
identically at base -- byte-identical after normalizing exactly those --
and 3 are the new fixture's interp/run/aot going red -> green. ZERO other
behaviour movers.

CANON: 9 movers, exactly the predicted set, with executable counts and
`tail dispatch` counts UNCHANGED on every one.
 +2 questions, +9 lines: 00231, 00281, opaque_fn_value_join,
   repr_seam_enum_count_after_reduce2 (one lambda over two inner
   closures now separates) and a_mixed.
 +4 questions, +18 lines: 00277.
 text only, 0 line delta: 00275, closure_identity_captures,
   enum_predicate_search -- capture types now print inside the question,
   id-free, no plan structure moves.
 a_mixed also RESEATS: the wide `closure[reduce#L](closure[each#L](any))`
   arm takes seat 0 ahead of the grounded one. Sound (the wide surface
   contains the narrow), output byte-identical, and the consequence is
   that the exact specialization x23 is emitted and unreachable --
   fz-kdt.168's shape, measured.

STRESS. `FZ_STRESS_PERMUTE_DISPATCH` over {arms:reverse, arms:1, arms:6,
wrappers:1, wrappers:6, 1, 6}: 0 stdout movers over the 9 canon movers
plus the two new fixtures on all THREE doors (GATE-1788379771), and 0
over the whole 594-fixture corpus on interp (GATE-1788379776).

WALL CLOCK (GATE-1788379906): nothing above 1s. Top of the corpus is
enum_take_drop_split 0.43s, 00420 0.41, 00277 0.29, enum_map_family 0.28,
enum_predicate_search 0.27 -- the same profile as base.

DELETED, verified by grep at PROOF-1788380509 (0 hits each): the
`captures: Vec::new()` erasure and the "captures leave no trace" doc;
`callable_boundaries_for_target` + its "has to admit all of them" doc;
`NativeCallableBoundary.target` and the surface's copy;
`NativeCallableBoundarySurface.capture_key`; the per-FnId agreement rule
and its message; the interp `CONSTRUCTION_WRAPPER_IDENTITY_BASE == 0`
exemption in `direct_callable_capture_lanes`;
`callables: FiniteSet<ClosureTarget>` as the axis field; the
`Fn(u64) -> Option<ClosureTarget>` resolver signature; the precision
row's "honest only while ... compiles on no path" caveat, in
runtime_type_predicate.rs and in dispatch-matrix.md;
`INDISTINGUISHABLE_ARM_RESIDUE` and
`compiler2_runtime_indistinguishable_arm_residue_stays_pinned` (the pin
would have asserted zero of nothing; its five fixtures moved up into the
zero gate instead). `a_nested_callables_captures_are_not_a_question` is
INVERTED to `..._are_a_question`, and
`runtime_indistinguishable_arms_keep_the_order_they_arrived_in` is
re-homed on `%{a: int}` vs `%{a: float}` -- a map test is a kind check on
an Erasing axis, so that pair really is one question. TWO `Vec::new()`
capture sites SURVIVE and are correct: `fn_ref_lit` (a fnref closes over
nothing) and the multi-literal clause in `callable_identity_clauses` (an
intersection is not one shape; naming its literals over no captures
over-approximates it, which is the direction a test must err in).

DOCS: dispatch-matrix.md's envelope paragraphs and nested example
rewritten, the precision row rewritten, a `CallableShapes` section added
beside the `TupleShapes` one stating the containment law;
types/mod.rs envelope doc; surface.rs; callsite_dispatch.rs
`question_groups`; pipeline.md's construction-identity paragraph gains
the fact that the boundary carries the shape and the unpack reads through
the minting wrappers. fz-kdt.125's record corrected by comment.

ONE SPEC ITEM NOT DONE, and it is a refuted premise rather than a cut --
see the comment on fz-kdt.127.2. The spec asked for a unit gate proving
the dynamic fixture GAINS a shape question at main's callsite. It does
not, at this stage, and the review's table row that said so was inferred,
not measured (there is no headB/sl3dyn.canon in the review's artifacts).
Measured here on BOTH dynamic variants: the head canon is byte-identical
to base's. `P.run/2` and `P.twice/2` stay one body each over the union,
the call to `f` is indirect through the value's own word, and the
construction wrapper's own member selection answers -- which is why the
program is correct at base. The gate written instead is the one that IS
observable and IS the cure:
`compiler2_a_forwarded_lambdas_capture_layout_is_the_runtime_question`
asserts the STATIC fixture's forwarder callsite carries two arms naming
one function whose questions are disjoint.

FOLDED the refutation's FIX-THEN-MERGE findings into the one commit.
AMENDED f34c2aaa3 -> 8c3d5ce900f3bfa85dcbeaf497c49addb2ff3862 on
wt/kdt127-1-build (parent still 172ab21f1). Ticket stays open.

F1 -- the multi-literal clause now degrades ONE way, by folding.
src/compiler2/types/mod.rs:2712 `callable_identity_clauses` no longer
splits a clause that pins several literals into its several literals over
NO captures; it keeps the CLAUSE SHAPE it was handed, literal for literal,
with every capture enveloped by the same reading. So how a clause projects
is decided in exactly one place -- `Types::runtime_type_predicate_callables`
(:1434) -- and the plan path (which envelopes first, callsite_dispatch.rs:781,
then projects the ENVELOPED ty, :386) reads what projecting the settled ty
would. The old split arrived there as EXACT zero-capture shapes, and
`CallableShape::inside` matches capture counts, so that axis refused every
CAPTURING construction of its own targets: under-admission, the direction a
test may never err in. The `identity(lit, Vec::new())` emission is gone;
`captures: Vec::new()` now occurs in types/mod.rs only at :1716, inside
`fn_ref_lit` (:1703), where a fn-ref genuinely has none.

RED-FIRST (marker RED2-1788383028, 2 failed):
  types_test.rs a_multi_literal_callable_clause_admits_every_capture_layout_of_its_targets
    -- "a clause it cannot shape must admit any capture layout of the
       targets it names"  FAILED
  types_test.rs the_envelope_and_the_predicate_agree_on_a_multi_literal_callable_clause
    -- left  CallableShapes { targets {66,68}, shapes [], exact false }
       right CallableShapes { targets {66,68}, shapes [#66(), #68()], exact true }
       FAILED
GREEN after the fold, marker GREEN1-1788383057 (2 passed).

Note for the record: the subject clause is `closure[66](int) &
closure[68](float)`, which the lattice calls semantically empty while both
projections still read its funcs -- consistent with the refutation's
measurement of 0 corpus hits on either degrade branch. Single-literal
clauses are byte-identical through the new code (`Conj { pos: vec![sig] }`
is what `Conj::pos_of` built), so the 9-mover canon result stands.

Docs corrected to the surviving truth: dispatch-matrix.md (both the :82
and the :301 sites now also say WHERE the decision is made and why the
split would under-admit) and the `callable_identity_clauses` doc.

F2 -- three unprovable doc claims rewritten.
  runtime_type_predicate.rs:797 `CallableShape::inside` -- "the lattice's
  own closure-literal subtyping" was wrong; it is capture-wise
  `RuntimeTypePredicate::contained_in`, containment of the projected TESTS
  and not of the semantic types they came from (that file's own :395).
  types/mod.rs `CallableReading::Identity` -- "Collapse it to callable
  IDENTITY" was residue of the retired doctrine; it now says it reduces to
  the CONSTRUCTION, identity plus capture types, dropping the arrow.
  types/mod.rs `runtime_envelope` -- "identity clauses OVER-approximate"
  now states the reason it is true (drops the arrow, widens each capture by
  the same reading, so it names at least what it replaced).

F3 -- fz-kdt.167's witness now ships here.
fixtures2/behavior/callable_union_capture_containment.fz (+ .oracle.exs,
.expected.txt), the refutation's F_mailbox_union_capture. A mailbox value is
typed `any`, so `mk` mints a construction whose capture is a UNION storing a
BOXED word, beside the same lambda's int and float constructions; one
forwarder carries all four. Oracle 12 / 11.0 / 12 / 11.0.
  GREEN on interp, JIT and AOT (marker FIX3-1788383222).
  RED-FIRST by swapping `CallableShapes::enumerates` to
  `shape.overlaps(ours)` (marker REDOVERLAP-1788383233):
    interp  12.0 11.0 12 11.0   -- WRONG on the first line
    JIT     abort, "fz_closure_get_capture_f64 expected float, got Int(1)",
            non-unwinding, exit 134
  Swap reverted; commented on fz-kdt.167, NOT closed.

F4 -- fz-kdt.170 filed (P1, bug, parent fz-kdt): a map-typed CAPTURE at two
value types answers 12.0 for 12 on interp and aborts on both native doors,
IDENTICALLY at base 172ab21f1 and here (marker K2-1788383303:
fz_ref_load_float ExpectedTag { expected: ValueKind(14), found:
ValueKind(13) }). Not a regression -- fz-kdt.131's map residue (a map's
runtime test is a KIND check, never the contents) reached through the
capture position this commit opened. Reproducer verbatim in the ticket and
kept at <scratch>/fold127.1/K2_map_capture.fz.

GATES, fresh, clean tree, markers quoted:
  GATE-1788383357   cargo fmt --check                      FMT-OK
                    cargo build --release (forced)         0 warnings
                    cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings CLIPPY-OK
  GATE-1788383387   cargo test --lib      1583 passed; 0 failed; 5 ignored
                                          (1581 + the 2 new F1 pins)
  GATE-1788383448   cargo test --test fixture_matrix -- --test-threads=1
                                          485 passed; 0 failed; 9 ignored
                                          (+3 lanes for the new fixture)
  GATE-1788383603   known-red set unchanged: matrix::{enum_tier0,
                    enumerable_protocol_dispatch, fz_f98_map_reduce}::
                    {run, interp, build}
  GATE-1788383751   the three behaviour fixtures on all three doors, each
                    byte-equal to its .expected.txt; and
                    `captures: Vec::new()` in types/mod.rs only at :1716
                    (fn_ref_lit).

title: fz-kdt.127 stage B: the callable axis names the construction, not the function -- CallableShapes, containment admission, PerPosition, construction-keyed capture unpack, on all three doors
